recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if a future work group decision reopens the broader Identifier namespace guidance; do not add redundant "no other system" wording now.
issue_request: FHIR-26438 was a Published/Persuasive MnM clarification for R5 asking to refine Identifier text about UUIDs by changing "for which no system has been assigned" to "for which no other system has been assigned".
initial_application: Commit 5cbc14c7d0f361941099bf72066b75c3f74f6d4f applied the issue in source/datatypes.html by replacing "no system has been assigned" with "no other system has been assigned" in the Identifier narrative.
additional_context: The current Identifier section is active build-scope source because source/fhir.ini lists Identifier as a reusable datatype and marks it normative. Later applied issues FHIR-45479, FHIR-41478, and FHIR-42959 rewrote the same area to clarify that an Identifier.system may be established for globally unique values, while urn:ietf:rfc:3986 is used when no assigned system exists and the value is expressed as a URI.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the obsolete phrase targeted by FHIR-26438 is no longer present and current source conveys the approved meaning.

related_jiras.note: Rewrote the Identifier globally unique value guidance and superseded the older "naturally globally unique" wording.
Merged with FHIR-45479 to clarify when OID/GUID values use urn:ietf:rfc:3986 versus a managed Identifier.system.
Clarified registry guidance for OIDs and UUIDs in the adjacent Identifier.system text.

evidence_items.summary: Current Identifier text states that globally unique values may have an established Identifier.system, and urn:ietf:rfc:3986 is used when no assigned system exists; fhir.ini lists Identifier as an active normative datatype.
